questions.stem: What is « le commerce équitable »?
questions.explanation: « Équitable » means fair, so this is trade that pays producers a fair price. Free trade, without tariffs, is « le libre-échange ».

questions.stem: « Née à Melbourne de parents libanais, Yasmine parle arabe chez elle, anglais au travail et français avec ses amis. Elle dit qu'elle est “un peu de partout”. » What does her comment suggest?
options: She would like to move to live in another country
She cannot decide which language to learn
She feels she belongs to several cultures at once
She feels she is at home nowhere at all
questions.explanation: « Un peu de partout » means 'a bit from everywhere', a positive sense of a mixed identity. Feeling at home nowhere would need a negative such as « de nulle part ».

questions.stem: What does « Les inégalités se creusent » mean?
questions.explanation: « Se creuser » means to deepen, like a hole being dug, so the gap is growing. It is a common verb in articles on social justice.

questions.stem: What is « un demandeur d'asile »?
questions.explanation: « Demander l'asile » is to apply for asylum. A job seeker is « un demandeur d'emploi », which shares the first word.

questions.stem: What is « la mondialisation »?
questions.explanation: « Le monde » gives « mondial » (worldwide) and « la mondialisation », the growing economic and cultural links between countries.

questions.stem: In an article on the Great Barrier Reef, what is « le blanchissement des coraux »?
questions.explanation: « Blanchir » means to turn white, and stressed corals lose their colour. Cleaning is « le nettoyage ».

questions.stem: What does « les feux de brousse » mean?
questions.explanation: « La brousse » is the bush, so this is the term French-language media use for Australian bushfires. Firefighters are « les pompiers ».

questions.stem: What is « l'Accord de Paris », signed in 2015?
options: a European treaty on the free movement of people
a peace agreement signed at the end of a world war
a trade agreement between France and its former colonies
an international agreement to limit global warming
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement, reached at the COP21 climate conference, commits countries to limit global warming. The free movement of people in Europe comes from the Schengen agreements.

questions.stem: « On nous répète qu'il suffit de trier nos déchets pour sauver la planète. Mais à quoi bon recycler si l'on continue à acheter toujours plus ? » What is the writer's position?
options: Buying more goods makes recycling more efficient
Sorting waste is the best way to save the planet
Recycling is not enough unless we also consume less
Recycling is useless and people should simply stop
questions.explanation: « À quoi bon » ('what is the point') questions recycling only on the condition « si l'on continue à acheter toujours plus ». The writer attacks overconsumption; nowhere do they say to stop recycling.

questions.stem: What does « la sécheresse » mean?
questions.explanation: « Sec » means dry, so « la sécheresse » is a long dry period. A heatwave is « une canicule », and a flood « une inondation ».

questions.stem: « Bien sûr, la voiture électrique pollue moins en ville. Encore faut-il produire l'électricité proprement et recycler les batteries. » What is the writer doing?
options: rejecting electric cars as worse than petrol ones
arguing that cities should ban every kind of car
explaining how batteries are recycled in France
accepting an advantage, then adding conditions that limit it
questions.explanation: « Bien sûr » concedes the benefit, and « encore faut-il » ('but then you still have to') adds the conditions for it to hold. This is evaluation, not a rejection of electric cars.

questions.stem: « Les jeunes sont de plus en plus sensibles à la cause environnementale. » What does « sensibles » mean here?
questions.explanation: « Sensible » is a false friend: it means sensitive or receptive. 'Sensible' in the English sense is « raisonnable ».

questions.stem: What is « la surconsommation »?
questions.explanation: The prefix « sur- » means 'over', as in « la surpopulation ». Consumer rights are « les droits des consommateurs ».

questions.stem: What is « la presse écrite »?
options: the freedom of the press in France
questions.explanation: « La presse écrite » is the print media, as opposed to radio, television and online news. Freedom of the press is « la liberté de la presse ».

questions.stem: What is « le hameçonnage »?
questions.explanation: « Un hameçon » is a fishhook, so the term mirrors English 'phishing': baiting people into giving up passwords. Spam is « le pourriel ».

questions.stem: What does « le temps d'écran » mean?
questions.explanation: « L'écran » is the screen, and the phrase is used in debates about young people and devices. A screen saver is « un économiseur d'écran ».

questions.stem: « Les influenceurs vendent du rêve, mais derrière chaque photo parfaite se cache souvent un partenariat rémunéré. » What does the writer imply?
options: Many of the 'perfect' posts are paid advertising
Influencers are paid too little for their work
questions.explanation: « Vendre du rêve » is to sell an unrealistic dream, and « un partenariat rémunéré » is a paid partnership with a brand, hidden (« se cache ») behind the image. The writer is criticising disguised advertising.

questions.stem: What is « un abonnement »?
questions.explanation: « Un abonnement » is the subscription itself; the person who holds it is « un abonné », which is also the word for a follower on social media.

questions.stem: « Le journal de 20 heures reste un rendez-vous pour des millions de Français, même si les jeunes s'informent de plus en plus sur leur téléphone. » Which statement matches?
options: Young people now watch the 8 pm news on their phones
The 8 pm news has lost most of its audience to phones
Phones have replaced television news for every age group
Many still watch the 8 pm news, though the young use phones more
questions.explanation: « Reste un rendez-vous » says the bulletin still draws a large audience, and « même si » concedes the shift among young people. Nothing says the news is watched on phones, or that its audience has collapsed.

questions.stem: In « la fabrication de voitures », what does « fabrication » mean?
questions.explanation: « La fabrication » is the making of something, and « fabriquer » means to manufacture. English 'fabrication' in the sense of a lie is a false friend here.

questions.stem: What is « le TGV »?
questions.explanation: TGV stands for « train à grande vitesse ». The Paris underground is « le métro ».

questions.stem: What does « le télétravail » mean?
questions.explanation: « Le télétravail » is working remotely, usually from home. Remote learning is « l'enseignement à distance ».

questions.stem: « Grâce aux progrès de la médecine, l'espérance de vie a beaucoup augmenté. Reste à savoir si nous vivrons plus longtemps en bonne santé. » What question remains?
options: whether life expectancy has really gone up at all
whether medicine has made any progress
how countries will pay for their health care
whether the extra years will be lived in good health
questions.explanation: « Reste à savoir » means 'it remains to be seen'. The first sentence accepts that life expectancy has risen; the open question is about quality of life.

questions.stem: What does « Le numérique est une arme à double tranchant » mean?
options: Digital technology doubles the speed of our work
Digital technology should be banned in schools
Digital technology has both benefits and dangers
Digital technology is mainly used by the military
questions.explanation: « Une arme à double tranchant » is a double-edged sword: it can cut both ways. The phrase is a useful frame for an evaluative piece.

questions.stem: In a persuasive article on the reef, which sentence describes a hypothetical outcome?
options: « La Grande Barrière de corail se trouve au large de la côte du Queensland. »
« Selon les scientifiques, les coraux souffrent de la hausse des températures. »
« L'année dernière, j'ai plongé sur la Grande Barrière avec ma classe de sciences. »
« Si nous n'agissons pas, nos petits-enfants ne verront jamais la Grande Barrière. »
questions.explanation: A si clause with a future result imagines what will happen if nothing changes, one of the persuasive strategies the study design names. The others give a fact, a source and a past experience.

questions.stem: What does « la fuite des cerveaux » mean?
questions.explanation: « La fuite » is an escape or leak, so this is the departure of skilled people to work abroad. It comes up in discussions of migration and higher education.

questions.stem: What does « le vivre-ensemble », a term with no single English equivalent, describe?
options: the official program for welcoming new migrants
people of all backgrounds getting along
the custom of adult children living with their parents
a shared house where several families live together
questions.explanation: « Le vivre-ensemble » is social cohesion in a diverse society: getting along across differences of culture, religion and background. It is an idea, not a housing or government program.

questions.stem: In an article on social justice, what does « la précarité » mean?
options: the speed of change in modern society
insecurity of work, income or housing
the high cost of living in big cities
the early retirement of older workers
questions.explanation: « La précarité » describes an unstable situation, such as short-term jobs or uncertain housing. « Un emploi précaire » is an insecure job.

questions.stem: What is « un eurodéputé »?
options: a member of the European Parliament
a deputy mayor of a French country town
a citizen of a European country
questions.explanation: « Un député » is a member of a parliament, so « un eurodéputé » sits in the European Parliament. A deputy mayor is « un adjoint au maire ».

questions.stem: What is « la transition énergétique »?
options: the shift from fossil fuels to cleaner energy
a sudden rise in the price of household electricity
the transport of energy across borders
a temporary cut to the power supply
questions.explanation: « La transition énergétique » is the move away from coal, oil and gas towards renewable and low-carbon sources. A power cut is « une coupure de courant ».

questions.stem: What are « les énergies fossiles »?
questions.explanation: « Les énergies fossiles » are coal, oil and gas. Renewable energies are « les énergies renouvelables ».

questions.stem: What does « la montée des eaux » mean?
questions.explanation: « La montée » is a rise, and « des eaux » refers to sea levels. It threatens low-lying islands in the Pacific and Indian Oceans.

questions.stem: What is « la décroissance »?
options: a fall in the birth rate of a country
an economic recession caused by a crisis
the gradual ageing of a population
choosing to produce and consume less
questions.explanation: « La décroissance » (degrowth) is a movement arguing that rich societies should choose to produce and consume less. A recession is an unwanted downturn, « une récession ».

questions.stem: What is « l'obsolescence programmée »?
options: the planned closure of old factories
designing products to wear out or date quickly
a computer program that updates itself
a schedule for replacing old public transport vehicles
questions.explanation: « L'obsolescence programmée » (planned obsolescence) is building a limited life into products so that consumers must replace them. It is a common target in arguments about waste.

questions.stem: What is « l'écoblanchiment », the official French term for an English word?
questions.explanation: « L'écoblanchiment » is presenting a product or company as greener than it is. Literally 'eco-whitewashing', it is the term recommended in place of 'greenwashing'.

questions.stem: What does « la liberté d'expression » mean?
questions.explanation: « L'expression » here is expressing opinions, so this is freedom of speech. Freedom of the press is « la liberté de la presse ».

questions.stem: What is « un lanceur d'alerte »?
questions.explanation: « Un lanceur d'alerte » is someone who reveals wrongdoing inside an organisation, literally 'someone who raises the alarm'. A fire alarm is « une alarme incendie ».

questions.stem: « Les algorithmes nous enferment dans une bulle : on ne voit plus que ce qui confirme nos opinions. » What is the writer's concern?
options: We spend too much time scrolling through social media
We only see content that confirms what we already think
Algorithms make it hard to find any information at all
Social media companies are selling our personal data
questions.explanation: « Enfermer dans une bulle » is to trap in a bubble, and « ne… plus que » means 'only any more'. The concern is the filter bubble, not data or screen time.

questions.stem: What does « une chercheuse » do?
questions.explanation: « Une chercheuse » (masculine « un chercheur ») is a researcher, from « la recherche ». « Chercher » also means to look for, which is the trap.

questions.stem: What are « les essais cliniques »?
questions.explanation: « Un essai » is a trial or test, and « clinique » refers to testing on patients. « Essai » can also mean an essay, but not with « clinique ».

questions.stem: What is Ariane?
options: a satellite navigation app made in France
questions.explanation: The Ariane rockets are built for the European Space Agency and launched from the space centre at Kourou in French Guiana. The high-speed train is the TGV.
